Policy Year

What it means, and what it does to a claim.

The twelve months running from your commencement date — not the calendar year, and not the financial year.

Why it matters

Every annual limit resets on this clock: your sum insured, your restoration, your health check-up entitlement. Two hospitalisations eleven months apart can fall in the same policy year and share one limit, while two a month apart can straddle the boundary and get a fresh one each. Knowing your commencement date is worth more than it sounds.

The legal definition

Policy Year means a period of twelve months beginning from the Commencement Date and ending on the last day of such twelve-month period. For the purpose of subsequent years, Policy Year shall mean a period of twelve months commencing from the end of the previous Policy Year and lapsing on the last day of such twelve-month period.

Aditya Birla Health — Activ One policy wording, UIN ADIHLIP27048V022627

Quoted verbatim from an IRDAI-filed policy wording. Definitions are standardised across insurers, but the limits attached to them are not — always read your own policy schedule.

Related terms

  • Policy Schedule — The document attached to your policy naming the insured persons, the sum insured, the policy period and the sub-limits your cover is actually subject to.
  • Renewal — Continuing the same policy for another term by paying the premium, keeping everything you have already accrued.
  • Sum Insured — The maximum the insurer will pay in a policy year.
